key_insight: ADACT jointly optimizes processor workload throttling and cooling to manage temperature while balancing execution throughput and cooling energy.
engineering_relevance: Physics-informed thermal control could help AI and HPC processors sustain performance under power-density and temperature constraints.
method: Model chip temperature with a 2D reaction–diffusion PDE, localized power sources, and variable convective cooling.
Discretize using Crank–Nicolson time stepping and a five-point spatial stencil.
Compute control gradients with a backward adjoint and optimize using L-BFGS.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports second-order forward and adjoint convergence verified by manufactured solutions, gradient checks via Taylor tests, and numerical experiments maintaining thermal thresholds and throughput.
watch_item: Evidence is numerical; real-time deployment and robustness to chip-model mismatch are not established in the abstract.
paper_title: ADACT: PDE-Constrained Thermal Hardware/Software Co-Design Adjoint-Driven Optimal Control via Finite Difference Discretization
